intended_object: For a right comodule M over a commutative R-bialgebra H, the n-th symmetric power Sym^n M, viewed as the degree-n homogeneous piece of the symmetric algebra Sym(M). It is a subcomodule of Sym(M) under the multiplicative coaction that extends the coaction of M. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The carrier is `SymmetricAlgebra.homogeneousSubmodule R M n`. It is defined as `(LinearMap.range ι)^n`, the R-span of products of exactly n generators, which is the standard degree-n part of Sym(M); for n = 0 it is the image of R.

`Subcomodule.ofSubmodule` attaches the stability proof. That proof shows the coaction of a degree-n element lies in the range of Sym^n M ⊗ H → Sym M ⊗ H, which is the usual definition of a subcomodule over a general base ring.

The coaction on Sym(M) is the algebra homomorphism determined by ι m ↦ ι m₍₀₎ ⊗ m₍₁₎. That is the standard comodule structure on the symmetric algebra of a comodule.

The setting is already general: R is any commutative semiring, M is any comodule, and no freeness or flatness is assumed. The only condition is that H be commutative, and the construction needs it: the coaction is built as an algebra map from the commutative algebra Sym(M) into Sym(M) ⊗ H, which requires Sym(M) ⊗ H, and so H, to be commutative. Mathlib has no subcomodule notion and no symmetric-power comodule, so there is no more general counterpart.
